notes.meaning: Jesus led Peter, James, and John up a high mountain so they could be alone. He chose three followers because God's law required two or three witnesses to confirm the truth of an event. These three were also being prepared by this special sight of His glory for the hard days of His suffering ahead.

Jesus' appearance changed completely right before their eyes. His face shone brightly like the sun, and His clothes became radiant and white as pure light. This was a glimpse of His divine glory, normally hidden beneath His ordinary human body, revealed to strengthen their faith.

other.label: Orthodox
other.view: Orthodox teaching holds that the light on the mountain was the uncreated, divine light of God Himself, showing human nature restored to its true beauty.

notes.meaning: Moses and Elijah suddenly appeared and began talking with Jesus about His coming death. Moses represented God's Law and Elijah represented the Prophets, and both came to honor Jesus and show that the whole Old Testament points to Him. Their presence also proved that God's people continue to live on with Him after leaving this world.

Peter was overwhelmed by the wonderful sight and offered to build three shelters of branches for Jesus, Moses, and Elijah. He spoke out of fear and excitement, wanting to stay in that safe, glorious place instead of facing the suffering Jesus had foretold. Without realizing it, Peter was also mistakenly putting Moses and Elijah on the very same level as his Lord.

A bright cloud of God's holy presence swept over them, and the Father spoke directly from heaven. God declared that Jesus is His dearly loved Son who brings Him complete joy, commanding the disciples to listen to Him above all others. This voice confirmed that Jesus is greater than Moses and Elijah and that His teachings carry God's own supreme authority.

Hearing God's holy voice filled the three disciples with dread, so they threw themselves facedown on the ground. Jesus came near, touched them with tender care, and told them to get up and not be afraid. His comforting touch and spoken word immediately took away their terror and restored their strength.

When the disciples looked up, the heavenly visitors were gone, and they saw only Jesus standing with them. The temporary glory of the Law and the Prophets had passed, leaving Jesus as their only Master and Savior. Christians must keep their eyes fixed on Christ alone for their comfort and guidance.

On the way down the mountain, Jesus ordered the three men to keep what they had seen completely secret until He had risen from the dead. If people heard about it before the cross, they would not believe it or would be confused by His coming death. After Jesus rose, this miraculous event would serve as powerful proof that He truly is the Son of God.

The disciples asked Jesus why the Jewish teachers taught that the prophet Elijah had to arrive before the Messiah. They had just seen Elijah vanish after only a few minutes, so they wondered how the ancient prophecy in Malachi was going to be fulfilled. They wanted Jesus to explain how this belief fit with what they had just seen.

Jesus confirmed that the Old Testament prophecy was right and that Elijah must come to prepare the way. This work meant turning people back to God by preaching repentance and calling them to reform their lives. Jesus did not come to discard the Scriptures, but to affirm their truth.

Jesus explained that the promised messenger had already arrived, but the religious leaders did not recognize who he was. Instead of receiving his message, they mistreated him and allowed him to be killed. In the very same way, wicked leaders would soon reject and execute Jesus.

The disciples then realized that Jesus was talking about John the Baptist. John came in the spirit and power of Elijah to prepare Israel for the Lord, matching what the prophets had written. By explaining this, Jesus cleared up their confusion and helped them see how God had kept His word.

When they reached the crowd below, a distressed man knelt before Jesus in humble respect. He came straight to Christ because his need was desperate and he knew only Jesus could help. A true sense of our helplessness will always bring us to our knees before the Lord.

The father begged for mercy because his son suffered from severe, life-threatening seizures. The boy was in terrible torment from an evil spirit that often threw him into fires or deep water to destroy him. It is right for loving parents to bring their sick and suffering children to Jesus in earnest prayer.

The father explained that he had asked the other nine disciples to drive out the demon, but they were unable to do it. Jesus allowed them to fail so they would stay humble and remember that their power came entirely from Him, not themselves. When human help fails, we must turn directly to Christ the Fountain of help.

Jesus rebuked the crowd and their leaders for their stubborn unbelief and twisted thinking. Even after seeing many miracles, the people still doubted His authority, which grieved Him deeply. Yet despite their sin, Jesus showed mercy to the boy and told the father to bring the child straight to Him.

Jesus commanded the demon to leave, and it immediately came out of the boy. The child was completely healed at that very second, freed from the torment that had lasted for years. Christ has total power over all the works of Satan, and no evil spirit can resist His word.

The disciples pulled Jesus aside into a private room to ask why their attempt had failed. They were confused because Jesus had previously given them authority over evil spirits. When our efforts for God seem to fail, we should quietly ask Him in prayer to reveal our weaknesses.

Jesus told them they failed because their faith was weak and they lacked real trust in the power He had given them. He said that even tiny faith, no larger than a mustard seed, could move mountains, meaning it can overcome seemingly impossible obstacles. The power does not come from our own strength, but from trusting God's promises.

This verse teaches that especially difficult and deeply rooted evil spirits can only be driven out through earnest prayer and fasting. Fasting helps humble the body and sharpens the soul so believers can pray with deeper focus and dependence on God. Believers need strong, active devotion to fight tough spiritual battles.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Scholars widely note that this verse is missing from the oldest Greek manuscripts of Matthew and was likely copied in later from Mark 9:29.

notes.meaning: While traveling privately through Galilee, Jesus warned His disciples again that He would be handed over to men who would put Him to death, but He would rise on the third day. His words filled the disciples with deep sadness because they loved Him and could not bear the thought of His death. Even though Jesus spoke clearly, their minds were clouded by the common expectation of an earthly, political Messiah.

In Capernaum, the men who collected the yearly two-drachma temple tax approached Peter to ask if Jesus paid it. This was not a tax for the Roman government, but an offering required by Jewish law to care for the temple in Jerusalem and its daily sacrifices. The collectors asked Peter politely, probably because they respected Jesus or were staying at Peter's home.

Peter answered at once that Jesus did pay the tax, and when he stepped inside the house, Jesus brought it up before Peter could speak. Jesus asked whether earthly kings collect taxes from their own children or from other people. By speaking first, Jesus showed His divine power to know thoughts and conversations even from a distance.

Peter replied that kings tax others, which led Jesus to conclude that a king's children do not have to pay. Since the temple is the house of God, Jesus, as God's true Son, was completely free from any duty to pay taxes for His Father's house. Even so, Jesus was willing to submit to humble duties during His time on earth.

differ.view: Believers are also exempt from this tax as adopted children of God, because Christ and His kingdom have replaced the old temple.
The exemption applies directly to Jesus alone as God's unique Son, and believers are free because the temple itself is passing away.

notes.meaning: To avoid causing offense or giving the impression that He looked down on the temple, Jesus agreed to pay the tax. He told Peter to catch a fish with a hook, promising that the very first fish would hold a four-drachma coin to cover the tax for both of them. This miracle showed Christ's complete control over creation and His faithful provision for those who follow Him.
